applies_why: The judge text decides whether D2-vs-C3 verses are unanswered witnesses and whether to keep a broken link, so it performs the K-G4 counting determination.
quote: so the "witness left unanswered" ground fails and the collision is regraded UNDERDETERMINED
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: Phrase: 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.' Readings weighed: (1) an answered verse must be excluded even if the retraction line is malformed; (2) the verse may still count unless the retraction quotes the pressing sentence and names the round. I adopt reading (1).
why: The judge text treats the witnesses as answered and removes the unanswered-witness ground, which is exactly the not-counting the rule permits.
